scr_budgeting_account_group_examples.purpose: Worked examples of account groups — Total Rental Revenue (GPR less vacancy, concessions and bad debt), Controllable Expenses, Total Operating Expenses and NOI — showing how members and signs combine into owner-style subtotals.
scr_budgeting_account_group_examples.outcome: Accountants can build or check groups that produce the NOI and expense subtotals asset managers expect.
scr_budgeting_account_group_examples.rootCause: Getting sign conventions wrong (adding concessions instead of subtracting) is the most common account group error and silently overstates revenue on every report built from the group.
scr_budgeting_account_group_examples.ifSkipped: Groups are built with wrong signs and revenue or NOI is misstated in owner packages.
redFlags: Contra-revenue accounts added rather than subtracted

scr_budgeting_account_groups_and_normal_.purpose: Explains how an account group's normal balance (debit or credit) determines whether members display as positive or negative, so revenue shows positive and expenses show positive in their own sections.
scr_budgeting_account_groups_and_normal_.outcome: Report subtotals display with the sign conventions owners expect.
scr_budgeting_account_groups_and_normal_.rootCause: Revenue accounts carry credit balances in the ledger. Without a credit normal balance on the revenue group, revenue shows as negative and NOI formulas invert.
scr_budgeting_account_groups_and_normal_.ifSkipped: Revenue appears negative, NOI calculations flip sign and owner reports look wrong.
redFlags: Revenue groups with debit normal balance

scr_budgeting_organize_through_account_g.purpose: Describes using account groups to organize accounts for different audiences — an owner view, a lender view, a management view — without changing the chart of accounts.
scr_budgeting_organize_through_account_g.outcome: One chart of accounts serves multiple reporting formats.
scr_budgeting_organize_through_account_g.rootCause: Lenders, JV partners and asset managers each want different groupings (lenders may exclude capex from opex; owners may want R&M split). Groups provide these views without duplicate charts.
scr_budgeting_organize_through_account_g.ifSkipped: Separate reports are built by hand for each audience, with inconsistent numbers.
redFlags: Lender NOI group including items the loan agreement excludes

scr_budgeting_multi_entity_report_struct.purpose: Multi-Entity Report Structures (a Multi-Entity Shared subscription) let account groups and report structures be shared across entities, so a portfolio of separate legal entities reports on one consistent structure.
scr_budgeting_multi_entity_report_struct.outcome: Portfolio and fund-level reports roll up consistently across entities.
scr_budgeting_multi_entity_report_struct.rootCause: Institutional portfolios hold each property in its own LLC. Consolidated or fund-level reporting needs identical structures in every entity, which is impractical to maintain entity by entity.
scr_budgeting_multi_entity_report_struct.ifSkipped: Each entity's structure drifts and fund-level roll-ups do not tie.
redFlags: Entities using local report structures instead of shared ones

scr_budgeting_importing_account_groups.purpose: Imports and exports account group definitions from templates — used when onboarding a new owner's reporting structure or copying groups between companies.
scr_budgeting_importing_account_groups.outcome: A new owner's reporting hierarchy is loaded accurately in one step.
scr_budgeting_importing_account_groups.rootCause: New management contracts come with the owner's required reporting structure. Keying dozens of groups by hand is error-prone; import reproduces the structure exactly.
scr_budgeting_importing_account_groups.ifSkipped: Owner reporting structures are keyed manually with errors and the first owner package is wrong.
redFlags: Imported groups not tested against a sample report

scr_budgeting_importing_account_group_me.purpose: Imports the GL account membership of account groups from a template, assigning many accounts to groups at once.
scr_budgeting_importing_account_group_me.outcome: Group memberships are populated or updated in bulk.
scr_budgeting_importing_account_group_me.rootCause: When a chart of accounts changes (new owner mapping, new accounts), many group memberships change together; bulk import avoids missing accounts.
scr_budgeting_importing_account_group_me.ifSkipped: Accounts are left out of groups and their balances vanish from subtotals.
redFlags: Accounts with balances not in any group

scr_budgeting_viewing_the_account_groups.purpose: Opens the Account Groups list to see all groups and their types, as the starting point for maintaining reporting structures.
scr_budgeting_viewing_the_account_groups.outcome: A full view of existing groups before creating new ones.
scr_budgeting_viewing_the_account_groups.rootCause: Reviewing existing groups first prevents duplicate NOI or revenue groups that would give different answers in different reports.
scr_budgeting_viewing_the_account_groups.ifSkipped: Duplicate groups are created and reports disagree.
redFlags: Several groups with near-identical names

scr_budgeting_account_groups_list.purpose: The Account Groups list with two views (list and hierarchy) for adding, editing, exporting and deleting groups.
scr_budgeting_account_groups_list.outcome: Groups are maintained from one place with visibility of their hierarchy.
scr_budgeting_account_groups_list.rootCause: The hierarchy view shows how a change to one group ripples up to NOI and net income, which the flat list does not.
scr_budgeting_account_groups_list.ifSkipped: Changes are made without seeing their effect on higher-level totals.
redFlags: Groups not placed in any hierarchy

scr_budgeting_account_groups_workflow.purpose: Describes the typical workflow: start from system account groups in the library, adjust memberships for the owner's chart, build hierarchies, then attach groups to financial reports and budgets.
scr_budgeting_account_groups_workflow.outcome: Reporting structures are built in a sensible order.
scr_budgeting_account_groups_workflow.rootCause: Building reports before groups are finalized leads to reports that must be rebuilt when group definitions change.
scr_budgeting_account_groups_workflow.ifSkipped: Reports are rebuilt repeatedly as groups change.
redFlags: Reports built on draft groups

scr_budgeting_adding_an_account_group.purpose: Creates an account group — name, type, normal balance, calculation method (for period, year-to-date or as-of balance) and member accounts.
scr_budgeting_adding_an_account_group.outcome: A new subtotal available to reports and budgets.
scr_budgeting_adding_an_account_group.rootCause: New owner reporting lines (e.g., separate 'Turnover Costs' subtotal) require new groups; the calculation method determines whether the group reports activity or balances.
scr_budgeting_adding_an_account_group.ifSkipped: Owners' requested subtotals cannot be produced.
redFlags: Wrong calculation method for balance sheet groups

scr_budgeting_setting_up_a_computation_a.purpose: Sets up a computation group whose value is a formula over other groups — NOI = Total Revenue − Total Operating Expenses, or expense per unit = Total Opex ÷ Units.
scr_budgeting_setting_up_a_computation_a.outcome: Key metrics like NOI and per-unit costs calculated consistently in every report.
scr_budgeting_setting_up_a_computation_a.rootCause: NOI and per-unit metrics drive valuation and benchmarking. Defining them once as formulas guarantees every report uses the same calculation.
scr_budgeting_setting_up_a_computation_a.ifSkipped: NOI and ratios are calculated by hand and differ between reports.
redFlags: NOI formula including depreciation or interest

scr_budgeting_viewing_and_editing_accoun.purpose: Views or edits an account group — including finding accounts missing from it — when a report subtotal does not match the trial balance.
scr_budgeting_viewing_and_editing_accoun.outcome: Group memberships are corrected so subtotals are complete.
scr_budgeting_viewing_and_editing_accoun.rootCause: When new accounts are added to the chart but not to groups, their balances silently drop out of report totals. Editing groups is how that is fixed.
scr_budgeting_viewing_and_editing_accoun.ifSkipped: Report totals exclude new accounts and do not tie to the trial balance.
redFlags: Report totals not tying to trial balance

scr_budgeting_adding_a_missing_account_t.purpose: Adds an account that was left out of a group — typically a newly created GL account — so its balance is included in subtotals.
scr_budgeting_adding_a_missing_account_t.outcome: Subtotals include all relevant accounts and tie to the trial balance.
scr_budgeting_adding_a_missing_account_t.rootCause: Adding accounts to the chart does not automatically add them to groups; each new account must be placed in the reporting structure.
scr_budgeting_adding_a_missing_account_t.ifSkipped: The new account's activity is invisible in owner reports.
redFlags: Accounts with balances in no group

scr_budgeting_deleting_an_account_group.purpose: Deletes an account group that no report, budget or other group uses — typically a duplicate or a group built for an owner who is no longer managed.
scr_budgeting_deleting_an_account_group.outcome: Obsolete groups removed without breaking reports.
scr_budgeting_deleting_an_account_group.rootCause: Unused groups clutter the structure and are selected by mistake when building reports; groups in use are protected from deletion.
scr_budgeting_deleting_an_account_group.ifSkipped: Obsolete groups are used in new reports, producing wrong subtotals.
redFlags: Duplicate groups retained

scr_budgeting_exporting_from_the_account.purpose: Exports account groups and their members to a file for review, documentation or transfer.
scr_budgeting_exporting_from_the_account.outcome: Reporting structure documented for owners, auditors or another company.
scr_budgeting_exporting_from_the_account.rootCause: Owners and auditors ask how report lines are built; an export of groups and members is the documentation.
redFlags: No documentation of NOI definition

scr_budgeting_account_to_account_group_m.purpose: The flip view of account groups: for each GL account it shows every group the account belongs to, so accounts in no group or in conflicting groups stand out.
scr_budgeting_account_to_account_group_m.outcome: Accounts missing from groups — or in conflicting groups — are easy to spot.
scr_budgeting_account_to_account_group_m.rootCause: An account in both 'Controllable' and 'Non-controllable' groups double-counts; an account in neither disappears. The flip view shows both problems.
scr_budgeting_account_to_account_group_m.ifSkipped: Double-counted or missing accounts distort reports.
redFlags: Accounts in mutually exclusive groups

scr_budgeting_viewing_how_accounts_are_m.purpose: Procedure for using the flip view to review how each GL account maps into account groups — normally done after chart of accounts changes or before a new owner's first report.
scr_budgeting_viewing_how_accounts_are_m.outcome: Mapping review completed before reports are published.
scr_budgeting_viewing_how_accounts_are_m.rootCause: A periodic mapping review, especially after chart changes, is how structural reporting errors are caught.
scr_budgeting_viewing_how_accounts_are_m.ifSkipped: Structural mapping errors persist for months and distort every report built on the groups.
redFlags: No mapping review after chart changes

scr_budgeting_account_group_information_.purpose: The record page for an account group — name, type, normal balance, calculation method, members and report filters.
scr_budgeting_account_group_information_.outcome: A complete definition of one subtotal.
scr_budgeting_account_group_information_.rootCause: Every attribute on this page changes the numbers on reports; reviewers need to see the full definition to trust a subtotal.
scr_budgeting_account_group_information_.ifSkipped: Subtotal definitions stay opaque and reviewers cannot verify how NOI or opex were built.
redFlags: Groups without descriptions

scr_budgeting_account_group_managers.purpose: Explains account group managers — people assigned responsibility for the accounts in a group (e.g., the maintenance director for R&M) for budgeting and variance accountability.
scr_budgeting_account_group_managers.outcome: Each budget area has a named owner responsible for variances.
scr_budgeting_account_group_managers.rootCause: Variance explanations are faster and better when a named person owns each area; without ownership, variance notes are vague.
scr_budgeting_account_group_managers.ifSkipped: Nobody owns variances and explanations are generic.
redFlags: Groups with no manager assigned

scr_budgeting_creating_an_account_group_.purpose: Assigns a manager to an account group so they receive budget and variance responsibility for it.
scr_budgeting_creating_an_account_group_.outcome: A named person accountable for each area's budget.
scr_budgeting_creating_an_account_group_.rootCause: Assigning managers enables routing of budget review and variance questions to the right person.
scr_budgeting_creating_an_account_group_.ifSkipped: Budget questions go to the wrong people.
redFlags: Managers assigned to groups outside their responsibility

scr_budgeting_editing_an_account_group_m.purpose: Updates who is assigned as manager of an account group (e.g., the R&M group moves to a new maintenance director), so budget and variance questions route to the right person.
scr_budgeting_editing_an_account_group_m.outcome: Budget responsibility stays with current staff.
scr_budgeting_editing_an_account_group_m.rootCause: Turnover at property and regional level is frequent; stale assignments route budget questions to people who have left.
scr_budgeting_editing_an_account_group_m.ifSkipped: Variance questions go to people who have left and remain unanswered at month-end.
redFlags: Assignments to terminated users

scr_budgeting_deleting_an_account_group_.purpose: Removes an account group manager assignment that no longer applies, for example after a regional reorganization that consolidated two maintenance territories.
scr_budgeting_deleting_an_account_group_.rootCause: Outdated assignments confuse routing of budget reviews and variance requests, especially after reorganizations.
scr_budgeting_deleting_an_account_group_.ifSkipped: Budget review and variance requests are routed to the wrong people after reorganizations.
redFlags: Groups left without any manager after deletion

scr_budgeting_adding_an_account_group_to.purpose: Adds an account group as a row in a financial report so its subtotal appears in the owner's income statement or BVA.
scr_budgeting_adding_an_account_group_to.outcome: Reports show the subtotals owners require.
scr_budgeting_adding_an_account_group_to.rootCause: Report rows are built from groups; adding the right group is how a requested subtotal (e.g., 'Total Turnover Costs') appears.
scr_budgeting_adding_an_account_group_to.ifSkipped: Requested subtotals are missing from owner reports.
redFlags: Groups added twice to the same report

scr_budgeting_report_filters_on_the_acco.purpose: Report filters on an account group restrict which books, locations or dimensions the group includes when used in reports.
scr_budgeting_report_filters_on_the_acco.outcome: Groups can be limited, for example to the accrual book only.
scr_budgeting_report_filters_on_the_acco.rootCause: Without book filters, a group can sum GAAP adjustments and accrual activity together, double-counting.
redFlags: Groups without book filters in multi-book companies

scr_budgeting_account_groups_library.purpose: The library of system-provided account groups (standard multifamily structures such as revenue, operating expenses and NOI) that can be installed and adapted.
scr_budgeting_account_groups_library.outcome: A tested starting structure instead of building groups from scratch.
scr_budgeting_account_groups_library.rootCause: Building a full reporting hierarchy from scratch is slow and error-prone; system groups provide a standard base.
scr_budgeting_account_groups_library.ifSkipped: Companies build inconsistent structures from scratch.
redFlags: System groups installed without adapting to the owner's chart

scr_budgeting_viewing_the_accounts_group.purpose: Browses the account groups library to see which standard groups are available and installed.
scr_budgeting_viewing_the_accounts_group.outcome: Users know which standard structures they can use.
scr_budgeting_viewing_the_accounts_group.rootCause: Knowing which standard groups already exist — and which are installed — prevents accountants from building custom duplicates that produce slightly different subtotals from the system versions.
scr_budgeting_viewing_the_accounts_group.ifSkipped: Custom groups duplicate standard ones and reports disagree on totals.
redFlags: Duplicates of standard groups

scr_budgeting_installing_system_account_.purpose: Installs selected standard account groups from the library (e.g., the system revenue, operating expense and NOI groups) into the company so standard reports and performance cards have their subtotals.
scr_budgeting_installing_system_account_.outcome: Standard groups available for reports and budgets.
scr_budgeting_installing_system_account_.rootCause: Many standard reports depend on system groups being installed; without them the reports show blank rows.
scr_budgeting_installing_system_account_.ifSkipped: Standard reports show blank or missing subtotal rows.
redFlags: Installed groups missing accounts specific to the owner

scr_budgeting_account_groups_hierarchy_r.purpose: Shows the full account group hierarchy with values — how accounts roll into groups and groups into totals — for a period.
scr_budgeting_account_groups_hierarchy_r.outcome: A visual check that the reporting structure produces the right totals.
scr_budgeting_account_groups_hierarchy_r.rootCause: Hierarchy errors (groups in the wrong parent, missing children) are easiest to spot with values shown at each level.
scr_budgeting_account_groups_hierarchy_r.ifSkipped: Hierarchy errors such as a group under the wrong parent reach owner reports.
redFlags: Totals at the top not matching net income

scr_budgeting_customizing_and_running_th.purpose: Sets parameters (groups, period, locations) and runs the Account Groups Hierarchy report.
scr_budgeting_customizing_and_running_th.outcome: A hierarchy report scoped to the structure under review.
scr_budgeting_customizing_and_running_th.rootCause: Reviewing one branch at a time (e.g., operating expenses) makes structural issues easier to see.
scr_budgeting_customizing_and_running_th.ifSkipped: Structure reviews are unfocused and errors in one branch are overlooked.
redFlags: Report run on the wrong book

scr_budgeting_viewing_a_monthly_report.purpose: Views the hierarchy report broken down by month to see how each group's value changed across the year.
scr_budgeting_viewing_a_monthly_report.outcome: Monthly trends by group, useful for budget seeding and seasonality.
scr_budgeting_viewing_a_monthly_report.rootCause: Budgets must reflect seasonality (utilities, turnover); monthly views by group show those patterns.
scr_budgeting_viewing_a_monthly_report.ifSkipped: Budgets spread amounts evenly and miss seasonality.
redFlags: Seasonal lines budgeted flat

scr_budgeting_account_groups_hierarchy_r.purpose: Explains the hierarchy report columns — group name, hierarchy level, values by period and totals — used to trace how each group rolls into its parent.
scr_budgeting_account_groups_hierarchy_r.outcome: Correct interpretation of the hierarchy output.
scr_budgeting_account_groups_hierarchy_r.rootCause: Reading the level column correctly tells the reviewer which parent subtotal a value rolls into, which is how misplaced groups (a below-NOI item inside NOI) are identified.
scr_budgeting_account_groups_hierarchy_r.ifSkipped: Values are attributed to the wrong subtotal.
redFlags: Levels not matching the intended structure

scr_budgeting_periodic_tasks.purpose: Periodic Tasks section of budgeting — creating, modifying, uploading and reporting on budgets through the annual cycle.
scr_budgeting_periodic_tasks.outcome: The budget cycle tasks are grouped for the budget season.
scr_budgeting_periodic_tasks.rootCause: Budget work is periodic (annual build, mid-year reforecast); grouping the tasks supports the cycle.
scr_budgeting_periodic_tasks.ifSkipped: Budget cycle steps are missed and the approved budget is not loaded before January reporting.
redFlags: Budget not loaded before January close

scr_budgeting_budgets_list.purpose: Lists all budgets (by year, version and status) with actions to create, view, modify, export, upload and delete them.
scr_budgeting_budgets_list.outcome: A register of budget versions showing which is approved for BVA reporting.
scr_budgeting_budgets_list.rootCause: Multiple versions exist each year (draft, revised, approved, reforecast). BVA must use the approved version; the list is where that is controlled.
scr_budgeting_budgets_list.ifSkipped: BVA reports use the wrong budget version.
redFlags: Several versions flagged as current

scr_budgeting_viewing_the_budgets_list.purpose: Opens the budgets list to confirm which budget versions exist and which is designated for reporting.
scr_budgeting_viewing_the_budgets_list.outcome: Clarity on which version BVA reports will use.
scr_budgeting_viewing_the_budgets_list.rootCause: Before running BVA or loading changes, the accountant must know which version is live.
scr_budgeting_viewing_the_budgets_list.ifSkipped: Changes are applied to the wrong version.
redFlags: Approved version not identifiable

scr_budgeting_adding_a_budget.purpose: Creates a new budget, either blank or based on an existing budget or actuals, for a fiscal year and set of locations.
scr_budgeting_adding_a_budget.outcome: A new budget version ready to populate.
scr_budgeting_adding_a_budget.rootCause: Each fiscal year and each reforecast needs its own version so the approved budget is never overwritten.
scr_budgeting_adding_a_budget.ifSkipped: The approved budget is overwritten during reforecasts.
redFlags: Reforecast built by editing the approved budget

scr_budgeting_creating_a_budget_manually.purpose: Builds a budget by typing amounts directly by account and month, used for small properties, special projects or a handful of lines where a model or import is unnecessary.
scr_budgeting_creating_a_budget_manually.outcome: A budget created directly in the system, typically for small properties or specific lines.
scr_budgeting_creating_a_budget_manually.rootCause: Some budgets (small properties, special projects) are simple enough to enter directly; manual entry must still be checked for seasonality and completeness.
scr_budgeting_creating_a_budget_manually.ifSkipped: Small budgets are kept outside the system and BVA cannot run.
redFlags: Annual totals keyed into one month

scr_budgeting_creating_a_budget_by_modif.purpose: Creates a new budget by copying an existing budget and applying changes — the common way to build next year's budget from this year's or a reforecast from the approved budget.
scr_budgeting_creating_a_budget_by_modif.outcome: A new version that keeps structure and only changes what should change.
scr_budgeting_creating_a_budget_by_modif.rootCause: Most budget lines carry forward with escalators; copying preserves structure and reduces effort while protecting the original.
scr_budgeting_creating_a_budget_by_modif.ifSkipped: Budgets are rebuilt from scratch with inconsistent structure.
redFlags: Copied budgets not updated for known changes (tax reassessment)

scr_budgeting_viewing_existing_budgets.purpose: Views loaded budgets at account or detail level to confirm that what is in the system matches the owner-approved budget file, total by total.
scr_budgeting_viewing_existing_budgets.outcome: Loaded budgets verified against the approved file.
scr_budgeting_viewing_existing_budgets.rootCause: After loading, the system budget must match the owner-approved budget; viewing it is the check.
scr_budgeting_viewing_existing_budgets.ifSkipped: Load errors go unnoticed until BVA looks wrong.
redFlags: System totals different from approved file totals

scr_budgeting_viewing_budget_details.purpose: Views the budget amounts by account and month for one location, to check monthly phasing of items like insurance, taxes and seasonal utilities.
scr_budgeting_viewing_budget_details.outcome: Monthly budget amounts can be checked line by line.
scr_budgeting_viewing_budget_details.rootCause: Monthly phasing matters for BVA; an annual amount in the wrong month creates large monthly variances.
scr_budgeting_viewing_budget_details.ifSkipped: Phasing errors produce misleading monthly variances.
redFlags: Annual items budgeted in one month instead of monthly accrual

scr_budgeting_exporting_a_budget_to_be_v.purpose: Exports a budget to a spreadsheet so the asset manager or regional manager can review it offline, clearly labeled with version and export date.
scr_budgeting_exporting_a_budget_to_be_v.outcome: Budget shared with reviewers in Excel.
scr_budgeting_exporting_a_budget_to_be_v.rootCause: Asset managers typically review budgets in Excel; the export must carry version identity to avoid confusion.
scr_budgeting_exporting_a_budget_to_be_v.ifSkipped: Budgets are shared by re-keying or screenshots, and reviewers comment on the wrong version.
redFlags: Exports without version labels

scr_budgeting_modifying_a_budget_manuall.purpose: Changes budget amounts manually in the budget details list — for example after the asset manager adjusts a line during review.
scr_budgeting_modifying_a_budget_manuall.outcome: Approved changes reflected in the system budget.
scr_budgeting_modifying_a_budget_manuall.rootCause: Review adjustments must be applied to the system version, or BVA uses a budget different from what the owner approved.
scr_budgeting_modifying_a_budget_manuall.ifSkipped: The system budget differs from the approved budget.
redFlags: Changes to the approved budget without approval evidence

scr_budgeting_uploading_changes_to_a_bud.purpose: Uploads a modified budget spreadsheet back into the system to apply many changes at once.
scr_budgeting_uploading_changes_to_a_bud.rootCause: Budget review cycles produce many line changes in Excel. Uploading applies them all accurately, whereas re-keying them invites errors that make the system budget differ from what the owner approved.
scr_budgeting_uploading_changes_to_a_bud.ifSkipped: Changes are re-keyed with errors or not applied.
redFlags: Upload totals not matching the approved file

scr_budgeting_deleting_budgets.purpose: Deletes a budget version, considering the implications for reports and comparisons that use it.
scr_budgeting_deleting_budgets.rootCause: Deleting a budget used in BVA or comparisons breaks those reports; only unused drafts should be deleted.
scr_budgeting_deleting_budgets.ifSkipped: Clutter; misuse deletes the approved budget.
redFlags: Deleting approved or prior-year budgets

scr_budgeting_troubleshooting_budget_imp.purpose: Guidance for resolving budget import errors — invalid accounts, locations, periods or formats in the upload file.
scr_budgeting_troubleshooting_budget_imp.outcome: Budget imports succeed without partial loads.
scr_budgeting_troubleshooting_budget_imp.rootCause: Import errors often cause partial loads where some lines load and others do not, leaving the budget incomplete without obvious signs.
scr_budgeting_troubleshooting_budget_imp.ifSkipped: Budgets are partially loaded and BVA shows false variances.
redFlags: Loaded totals lower than the file

scr_budgeting_budget_report.purpose: Analyzes budget information by account, location and period, with comparison to actuals where available.
scr_budgeting_budget_report.outcome: Budget detail and comparison for review and owner reporting.
scr_budgeting_budget_report.rootCause: Owners need budget detail by period to understand expected performance and later variances.
scr_budgeting_budget_report.ifSkipped: Budget detail must be assembled manually.
redFlags: Report run on the wrong budget version

scr_budgeting_customizing_and_running_th.purpose: Sets budget report parameters — budget version, period, locations, account groups — and runs it.
scr_budgeting_customizing_and_running_th.outcome: A budget report scoped to the review.
scr_budgeting_customizing_and_running_th.rootCause: Choosing the right budget version and groups ensures the report matches what the owner approved.
scr_budgeting_customizing_and_running_th.ifSkipped: Budget reports show the wrong version and owners see numbers they never approved.
redFlags: Draft version selected for owner reports

scr_budgeting_budget_report_columns.purpose: Explains the budget report columns — account, period budgets, totals and drill links.
scr_budgeting_budget_report_columns.rootCause: Drill links allow checking how a budget line was built; columns show phasing across periods.
scr_budgeting_budget_report_columns.ifSkipped: Phasing and build-up errors are missed until monthly variances appear.
redFlags: Uneven phasing on items that accrue evenly

scr_budgeting_budget_information_page.purpose: Page for adding a budget — name, fiscal year, locations, basis (blank, copy of a budget, or actuals).
scr_budgeting_budget_information_page.outcome: A budget shell defined correctly before amounts are entered.
scr_budgeting_budget_information_page.rootCause: Choosing the correct year, locations and basis up front avoids rebuilding the budget later.
scr_budgeting_budget_information_page.ifSkipped: Budgets are created for the wrong year or locations.
redFlags: Budget fiscal year different from the owner's fiscal year

scr_budgeting_budget_details_list.purpose: Lists budget amounts by account and period for a budget, where details are managed and edited.
scr_budgeting_budget_details_list.outcome: The line-level budget data maintained in one place.
scr_budgeting_budget_details_list.rootCause: BVA reports read from these details; errors here directly become BVA variance errors.
scr_budgeting_budget_details_list.ifSkipped: Line errors flow straight into every budget-vs-actual report for the year.
redFlags: Lines with zero budget on accounts with regular spend
